summary.headline: Welspun Enterprises H1 FY27 consolidated revenue up 11% to Rs 1,808 crore, EBITDA up 53% to Rs 610 crore, margin 32.4%.
summary.overview: Management reported H1 FY27 consolidated revenue from operations of Rs 1,808 crore (up 11% YoY) and EBITDA of Rs 610 crore (up 53% YoY), with EBITDA margin at 32.4% versus 23.9% in H1 FY26. Q2 FY27 standalone-style figures were cited as revenue around Rs 351 crore (up 179% YoY per the call) and EBITDA of Rs 296 crore, though the transcript is garbled and these Q2 numbers are unclear. Management reiterated FY27 guidance of 10-20% revenue growth and EBITDA margin of 18%+, and reported a DGH order allowing use of ONGC's existing facilities for its Mumbai block gas evacuation, expected to cut capital cost by USD 300-400 million. The Michigan (tunneling/engineering) segment's H1 revenue of about Rs 318 crore lagged the expected run rate, with order book at Rs 2,279 crore.

segments.name: Transportation (roads)
segments.commentary: Anta-Simaria road monetisation expected to be reflected in Q3 FY27 financials, with equity of about Rs 200 crore cited. Varanasi-Aurangabad road completed, provisional completion certificate awaited. Kanatham Puram-Nagapatnam at 90% completion. Pune-Shirur road: debt sanction of Rs 6,334 crore from NaCRD, Union Bank and PNB; financial closure and appointed date expected by Q4 FY27.

segments.name: Water
segments.commentary: 418 MLD treatment plant on track for commissioning by 20 July 2027, followed by a 15-year O&M contract. 2,000 MLD plant civil works resumed after disruptions from debris disposal restrictions and BMC suspension due to Mumbai air quality. Panjrapur 910 MLD plant in mobilisation and excavation, target completion April 2030. Dharavi-Ghatkopar tunnel shaft excavation at 26 m, completion by FY33. UP Jal Jeevan Mission over 80% physical completion, targeted for substantial completion in FY27.

segments.name: Oil and gas (ONGC/Mumbai block)
segments.commentary: DGH approved use of ONGC's existing facilities (B-12/11P platform, TPPP, SVHC pipeline, Hazira) for gas evacuation from the Mumbai block, held via Adani Welspun Exploration. Revised DPR submitted to DGH, awaiting approval; capex and revenue figures not yet disclosed.

segments.name: Specialised engineering and tunnelling (Michigan)
segments.commentary: H1 FY27 revenue about Rs 318 crore, with YoY moderation attributed to order release timing. Order book Rs 2,279 crore, about three years of run-rate; tunnelling about 53% and rehabilitation about 19% of mix per the call. Management expects Rs 700-1,200 crore of fresh orders in the next half. Dharavi-related TBM breakthrough on 9 October; several projects targeted for completion by FY27 and September 2027.

guidance_outlook: Revenue growth guidance of 10-20% for FY27 reiterated; management expects H2 to be stronger, as H1 typically is about 40% of annual revenue.
EBITDA margin guidance of 18%+ maintained; management says current margins are above 20% excluding one-offs.
Incremental order inflow target of Rs 8,000-10,000 crore in FY27, mainly water, rehabilitation and tunnelling, with transportation orders possibly by year-end.
Pune-Shirur road revenue expected at Rs 300-400 crore in FY27 and Rs 1,000-1,200 crore in FY28, subject to appointed date.
Michigan FY27 growth expected, though management did not confirm reaching the prior ~Rs 1,000 crore revenue expectation; medium-term guidance retained.
Medium-term Michigan EBITDA margin ambition of about 20%.
capex_capacity: DGH-approved ONGC facility usage for Mumbai block cuts capex by an estimated USD 300-400 million versus a longer pipeline to shore; revised DPR awaiting DGH approval.
Pune-Shirur road: test piling and site establishment underway, funding yards at two locations, financial closure expected Q4 FY27.
418 MLD plant commissioning 20 July 2027; Panjrapur 910 MLD completion April 2030; Dharavi-Ghatkopar tunnel completion FY33.
demand_pricing: Michigan order book Rs 2,279 crore, about three years of current run-rate; management guides to Rs 700-1,200 crore of new orders in the next half.

Management said it is not buying Chinese TBMs and sources from Japan and Germany, with makers having plants in Thailand and India; sees no impact from China's reported export curbs on tunnelling machines.
Management expects water and tunnelling orders to dominate the balance of FY27.

qa_highlights.question: What revenue and profitability can the oil and gas division contribute once operational, and what is the peak potential?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said details are partly confidential. Capex is expected to fall by USD 300-400 million by using existing ONGC infrastructure, and revenue depends on producible gas volumes and expected gas price. Exact figures to be shared after DGH approval of the revised DPR.

qa_highlights.question: Michigan H1 revenue was only about Rs 320 crore against an expected ~Rs 1,000 crore for the year; what is the H2 outlook?
qa_highlights.answer: Management attributed the moderation to order release timing, said orders have now been released, and expects FY27 to be a growth year, though it could not confirm reaching the prior target.

qa_highlights.question: Impact of China's reported tunnelling machine export curbs?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it has not bought Chinese TBMs and sources from Japan and Germany, with Thailand and India operations, so no impact is expected on project execution.

qa_highlights.question: Which sectors will the Rs 8,000-10,000 crore order inflow come from?
qa_highlights.answer: Water (including treatment) and rehabilitation and tunnelling orders are expected in the balance of FY27, with transportation orders possibly by year-end.

qa_highlights.question: Pune-Shirur road revenue for FY27 and FY28?
qa_highlights.answer: Rs 300-400 crore in FY27 depending on the appointed date, and Rs 1,000-1,200 crore in FY28 on current forecast.

qa_highlights.question: Does management stick to 10-20% revenue growth and 18%+ margin guidance after H1?
qa_highlights.answer: Yes. Management reiterated both, citing H1 at about 40% of annual revenue and current margins above 20%.

risks_watch: Michigan H2 revenue delivery versus target, given H1 was about Rs 318-320 crore and the order book depends on timely order releases.
Water execution delays from BMC/Mumbai air quality restrictions on debris disposal at the 2,000 MLD project.
Pune-Shirur road financial closure and appointed date slipping beyond Q4 FY27, which would push FY27 revenue below Rs 300-400 crore.
Oil and gas project: DGH approval of the revised DPR and final capex and revenue numbers still pending.
Anta-Simaria monetisation completion in Q3 FY27 and realised value.
Order inflow of Rs 8,000-10,000 crore in FY27 is a stretch relative to the Rs 700-1,200 crore Michigan guidance and the state of other segments.
summary.management_tone: Confident on consolidated profitability and guidance, but cautious and vague on Michigan H2 delivery and order timing; several answers were unclear or confidential. Management avoided giving hard numbers on the oil and gas revenue and capex.
key_quotes: Thank you for this question. I will be able to partly address this question because of some certain confidentiality issues.
We are reasonably confident that we will be in the guided range of 10 to 20% on the revenue growth.
So as I said I have maintained that our current margins are much higher even if we take away our margins are in the ranges of 20% plus.

rows.label: Volume growth

rows.label: Guidance upgrade

rows.label: Guidance downgrade
rows.why: Michigan H1 revenue of about Rs 318 crore lags the expected run rate, and Pune-Shirur FY27 revenue of Rs 300-400 crore depends on an appointed date not yet fixed.

rows.label: FY27 order inflow Rs 8,000-10,000 crore
rows.why: Management targets Rs 8,000-10,000 crore of orders mainly in water, rehabilitation and tunnelling, but guides Michigan to only Rs 700-1,200 crore of fresh orders in the next half against a Rs 2,279 crore order book.

rows.label: Anta-Simaria road monetisation

rows.label: DGH approval of revised DPR for Mumbai block

tone.note: Management was confident on consolidated profitability and held FY27 guidance, but cautious and vague on Michigan H2 delivery, order timing and oil and gas numbers; analysts pressed on Michigan's shortfall against the ~Rs 1,000 crore expectation.
